A1-dimensions.title: Known with derivation: the dimension comparison
A1-dimensions.statement:
\label{A1-dimensions}
We use orientation-preserving markings that preserve the peripheral
classes and labelled boundary circles; boundary points may move during
isotopy. The positive-boundary Teichm\"uller space of stable type $(g,n)$
has real dimension $6g-6+3n$. For a connected stable graph of total genus
$g$ with $n$ legs, its normalized component moduli together with a
nonzero complex tangent tensor at every edge have complex dimension
$3g-3+n$. Adding $n$ external positive cap parameters gives real
dimension $6g-6+3n$. These counts verify 67/077 and 67/016, but do not
establish existence or surjectivity of the proposed arrows.

A1-cap-bound.title: Known, with independent proof: the cap bound
A1-cap-bound.statement:
\label{A1-cap-bound}
Let $f:\D\longrightarrow\C\setminus\{1\}$ be injective and holomorphic, with $f(0)=0$. Then $|f'(0)|\leq4$. Thus a pointed disc in $\mathbf P^1$ centred at $0$ and avoiding $1,\infty$ has conformal radius at most $4$ in the coordinate $z$.

A1-tensor.title: Proved: the tensor produced by a toric seam
A1-tensor.statement:
\label{A1-tensor}
Let $f:\overline\D\to D_a\subset Y$ and $h:\overline\D\to D_b\subset Y$ parametrize two pointed analytic discs, with centres $a,b$. An orientation-reversing toric identification of their boundaries has the form $f(\zeta)\sim h(c/\zeta)$, $|\zeta|=1$, where $|c|=1$. Its tangent tensor is
\[
q=c\,df_0(\partial_\zeta)\otimes dh_0(\partial_\eta).
\]
In any chosen branch coordinates its modulus is the product of the two conformal radii.

A1-global-refutation.title: Refuted: the global isomorphisms in A.1 and L2
A1-global-refutation.statement:
\label{A1-global-refutation}
With the unrestricted nonzero-tensor target of cote 67/075--078,
the proposed global isomorphisms are false. For the geodesic-cut
interpretation the unbordered map is not surjective on complex objects,
already for $(g,n)=(0,4)$ and then for every stable type with
$3g-3+n>0$. The same cap-size obstruction rules out a preimage for
specified bordered target objects whenever the tensor is obtained
from the actual caps. This is an obstruction to coarse surjectivity
as well as to equivalence of stacks or groupoids. Under the external-only
admissibility reading the bordered arrow also has the separate failure
of being undefined on some objects, proved in
Proposition~\ref{A1-bordered-landing}; it must not be described simply
as a globally defined map with a proper image. For arbitrary embedded
cuts, Proposition~\ref{A1-nontoric-cut} supplies the earlier failure
of the tensor construction itself.

A1-zero.title: Proved: the zero-complexity edge case
A1-zero.statement:
\label{A1-zero}
For $(g,n)=(0,3)$ there is no essential stable cut. The unbordered groupoid with labelled markings is a point. The bordered capping functor is an equivalence with pointed spheres equipped with an admissible three-disc system, when admissible has its definition from 67/065--066 and arrows retain those discs.

A1-retained-discs.title: Proved: the corrected surgery equivalence
A1-retained-discs.statement:
\label{A1-retained-discs}
Fix a stable graph. Enlarge the target by retaining admissible pointed caps at every branch of every node, as well as at the external markings, and a toric boundary identification at every node. Require the two hyperbolic boundary lengths at a node to be equal. Then geodesic cutting and canonical capping give an equivalence of groupoids with hyperbolic bordered surfaces cut along that graph. The nodal tensor alone is a forgetful invariant of this equivalence.

A1-first-order.title: Known with derivation: the intrinsic first-order parameter
A1-first-order.statement:
\label{A1-first-order}
For an ordinary node with branches $a,b$ on a smooth normalization $Y$, the one-dimensional space of local first-order smoothings is canonically $T_aY\otimes T_bY$. Given analytic coordinates $x,y$ at the branches, the family $xy=t$ represents this identification by $t\,\partial_x\otimes\partial_y$. Coordinate choices enter at higher order. For a fixed stable complex curve, sufficiently small such parameters together with deformation parameters for the normalized pointed components give local analytic plumbing charts, modulo its finite automorphism group.

A1-cut-not-algebraic.title: Refuted: finite-type algebraicity of the natural cut component
A1-cut-not-algebraic.statement:
\label{A1-cut-not-algebraic}
Let $\mathcal D$ be a connected component of the moduli space of
four-labelled punctured spheres equipped with one essential
unoriented cut isotopy class, represented by its hyperbolic
geodesic. Give $\mathcal D$ its natural complex structure: forgetting
the locally constant cut class is a local biholomorphism to
$M_{0,4}^{\mathrm{an}}$.
Then
\[
 \mathcal D\simeq
 \mathbb H/\langle\tau\mapsto\tau+2\rangle
 \simeq\{q\in\C:0<|q|<1\}.
\]
In particular $\mathcal D$ is not the analytification of a smooth
connected finite-type algebraic curve over $\C$. Thus the natural
geodesic-cut source cannot be treated as a finite-type algebraic
moduli curve, and it cannot be algebraically isomorphic to the
corresponding unrestricted nodal-tensor stratum $\C^\times$.
This is a limitation of that specified algebraic interpretation;
it does not infer nonholomorphicity of the surgery map from its
real-analytic description.

A1-bordered-landing.title: Refuted: the bordered map lands in the stated target
A1-bordered-landing.statement:
\label{A1-bordered-landing}
Canonical cutting and capping need not produce an admissible system
of external discs on the normalization when the node caps are
forgotten and their centers are left as punctures. This already
fails for a four-holed sphere with one separating cut, all five
geodesic lengths---the four external boundaries and the cut---equal
to $2\pi$. Thus, with the componentwise admissibility just specified,
the displayed arrow $MDB\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{st}}ND$ of
67/076 is not a well-defined map on all objects.

A1-bordered-shadow-range.title: Proved: exact bordered model by tensors and shadows
A1-bordered-shadow-range.statement:
\label{A1-bordered-shadow-range}
On the fixed graph and normalization, record the nonzero node
tensors $q_e$ and the external cap shadows, of radii $r_l>0$.
Canonical cutting and capping gives a real-analytic diffeomorphism
from bordered cut surfaces, with actual toric seam phases, onto
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)=\biggl\{(q,r):\quad&
 \sum_{e\in E}p_e\log|q_e|+
 \sum_{l\in L}p_l\log r_l<K_{\Gamma,L}(p)\\
 &\text{for every }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\biggr\}.
\end{align*}
The logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed.
The source length at every edge or external leg is
$2\pi\sqrt{t_j}$, where $t$ is the unique solution
\[
 \nabla\Psi_{\Gamma,L}(t)
   =\bigl((\log|q_e|)_{e\in E},(\log r_l)_{l\in L}\bigr).
\]
Thus the node tensors and the external shadows determine all node
and external cap domains, all boundary lengths, and the cut surface.
The statement includes self-nodes and fixed cusp markings. Its
tangent map is an isomorphism; as the normalization varies, the
range forms an open real-analytic subbundle. The inclusion into
the full nonzero-tensor and positive-shadow bundle is an
equivariant homotopy equivalence.

A1-bordered-shape-image.title: Proved: the image when full external discs are retained
A1-bordered-shape-image.statement:
\label{A1-bordered-shape-image}
Replace the manuscript's external-only admissibility requirement
by arbitrary embedded pointed external discs with disjoint
analytic closures avoiding every other special point. The exact
image of canonical surgery in this target consists of the tuples
$(Y,(q_e),(D_l))$ satisfying both of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tensors and the shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ satisfy all support
inequalities of Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}.
\item Let $t$ be the unique gradient inverse furnished by that
theorem. On every component, the given external discs $D_l$ are
exactly the external members of the canonical full cap system
with squared length parameters $B_vt$.
\end{enumerate}
These conditions determine a real-analytic graph over
$\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$. They give a complete reconstruction
criterion, and do not require the retained external subsystem
to be admissible after the node caps have been discarded.

A1-nontoric-cut.title: Refuted: arbitrary analytic cuts canonically give toric cap identifications
A1-nontoric-cut.statement:
\label{A1-nontoric-cut}
If the cut circles in 67/074 are interpreted as arbitrary embedded
smooth, or even analytic, circles, cutting and canonical capping
does not always give the asserted antiisomorphisms of pointed caps.
This failure already occurs on a four-punctured sphere with one
separating circle. The geodesic-cut model used in
Theorems~\ref{A1-graph-range} and~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}
therefore requires geodesic representatives, or toric compatibility
together with equality of the paired hyperbolic boundary lengths.
Smoothness alone does not supply these conditions. Toric compatibility
without length equality defines the larger, noninjective model of
Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain}.

A1-welding-plumbing.title: Proved: toric welding is plumbing with the retained coordinate germs
A1-welding-plumbing.statement:
\label{A1-welding-plumbing}
For the corrected surgery data of Proposition~\ref{A1-retained-discs}, every seam is an ordinary analytic plumbing, using the coordinate germs supplied by its two pointed caps. This assertion identifies the welded surface itself. It does not identify the finite plumbing parameter, in a fixed independent choice of germs, with an arbitrary element of the whole normal tensor line.

A1-kra-comparison.title: Known with derivation: the scope of Kra's coordinates
A1-kra-comparison.statement:
\label{A1-kra-comparison}
Fix a maximal pants graph of type $(g,n)$ and put $d=3g-3+n>0$. Kra's horocyclic plumbing parameters range in a domain $D$ satisfying
\[
 \mathbb D_{e^{-2\pi}}^{d}\subset D
                   \subset\mathbb D_{e^{-\pi/2}}^{d}.
\]
They cover the moduli of surfaces of that type, generally many times. On marked Teichm\"uller space the logarithmic coordinates $\tau_j$ are global holomorphic coordinates on their image; the corresponding Dehn twist sends $\tau_j$ to $\tau_j+2$. After quotienting these twists, $t_j=e^{\pi i\tau_j}$ are the plumbing coordinates on $D\cap(\C^\times)^d$. They are not coordinates on an unrestricted normal-tensor bundle.

A1-wolpert-comparison.title: Known with derivation: Wolpert's metric comparison
A1-wolpert-comparison.statement:
\label{A1-wolpert-comparison}
The local family $xy=t$, $0<|t|<1$, is the annulus $|t|<|x|<1$. Its complete curvature-minus-one metric and core length are
\[
 ds_t^2=\left[
 \frac{\pi}{|\log|t||}
 \csc\!\left(\frac{\pi\log|x|}{\log|t|}\right)
 \left|\frac{dx}{x}\right|\right]^2,
 \qquad L_t=\frac{2\pi^2}{-\log|t|}.
\]
On compact subsets of either punctured limiting branch the metric tends to the cusp metric. For a degenerating family of compact stable curves, Wolpert's Expansion~4.2 compares the global hyperbolic metric with the interpolated cusp/annulus metric; its constants are local in the normalization parameters and coordinate germs. This supplies a metric comparison for plumbing, not a global inverse on normal tensors.

A1-hinich-counterexample.title: Known with an exact counterexample: arbitrary plumbing need not be a chart
A1-hinich-counterexample.statement:
\label{A1-hinich-counterexample}
Even for $(g,n)=(0,4)$, disjoint coordinate discs and the equation $xy=t$ do not ensure that the plumbing map is locally invertible at every nonzero parameter. An instance of Hinich's counterexample is obtained by
\[
 R=\tfrac32,\quad B=\tfrac34,\quad C=10,\quad
 A=\tfrac{420}{569},\quad \varepsilon=\tfrac1{10},
 \qquad \phi(z)=(z-R)^2.
\]
The critical plumbing parameter is $t=9/11$.

A1-graph-range.title: Proved: exact range, tangent map, and fundamental group
A1-graph-range.statement:
\label{A1-graph-range}
For the fixed normalization, the unbordered canonical surgery map,
with actual toric seam identifications as its phase variables, is a
real-analytic diffeomorphism onto
\[
 \mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)=
 \left\{(q_e)\in\prod_{e\in E}(T_{a_e}Y\otimes T_{b_e}Y)^\times:
   \sum_e p_e\log|q_e|<K_\Gamma(p)
   \quad\text{for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^E\right\}.
\]
Its logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed.
If $E\ne\varnothing$, this is a proper subset of the unrestricted
nonzero-tensor fiber. The tangent map of surgery is an isomorphism.

As the normalization varies on its fixed graph stratum, these images
form an open real-analytic subbundle of the nonzero-tensor bundle.
Its inclusion is an equivariant homotopy equivalence, and consequently
induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, including orbifold
fundamental groups when finite automorphisms are retained. These
conclusions allow loop edges as well as edges between different
components.

A1-small-ranges.title: Proved: the two smallest one-node ranges
A1-small-ranges.statement:
\label{A1-small-ranges}
For the separating one-node $(0,4)$ curve, normalize each rational
component by putting its node at $0$ and its two external markings at
$1,\infty$. In the resulting tensor frame the exact range is
\[
                         0<|q|<16.
\]
For the irreducible one-node $(1,1)$ curve, put its two branches at
$0,1$ and its marking at $\infty$ on its rational normalization.
In the frame $\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_z|_1$ the exact range is
\[
                         0<|q|<1.
\]
In both cases every phase occurs and the length is uniquely determined
by $|q|$.

A2-schwarzian.title: Known with independent derivation: projective connection of a capped pant
A2-schwarzian.statement:
\label{A2-schwarzian}
Let a hyperbolic pant have boundary lengths $\ell_0,\ell_1,\ell_\infty>0$, and canonically cap it at the three boundaries. Normalize the resulting sphere by placing the cap centres at $0,1,\infty$. Set
\[
a_j=\frac12\left(1+\frac{\ell_j^2}{4\pi^2}\right).
\]
The hyperbolic developing map extends as a complex projective structure to the punctured capped sphere, whose Schwarzian in the coordinate $z$ is
\[
T(z)=\frac{a_0}{z^2}+\frac{a_1}{(z-1)^2}
       +\frac{a_\infty-a_0-a_1}{z(z-1)}.
\]
If $u$ is any centred unit-disc coordinate on the cap at $0$, write $u(z)=c z(1+bz+O(z^2))$. Then
\[
b=\frac{a_0+a_1-a_\infty}{2a_0}.
\]

A2-independence.title: Refuted: the independence asked in 67/068
A2-independence.statement:
\label{A2-independence}
In a canonically capped pant the cap at $0$ need not depend only on $\ell_0$. In particular, the pants with length triples $(2\pi,2\pi,2\pi)$ and $(2\pi,4\pi,2\pi)$ have different caps at $0$ in the common normalization $0,1,\infty$.

A2-cusp-norm.title: Known with derivation: cusp norms and decorations
A2-cusp-norm.statement:
\label{A2-cusp-norm}
For a compact pointed complex curve $(Y,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete hyperbolic metric on $Y\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines canonical Hermitian norms on $T_{p_i}Y$. If $q_i$ is its cusp coordinate, then
\[
 ds^2=\frac{|dq_i|^2}{|q_i|^2\log^2|q_i|},\qquad
 \|v\|_{p_i}=|dq_i(v)|.
\]
The coordinate is unique up to a constant of modulus one. A horocycle of circumference $h_i$ has coordinate radius $\exp(-2\pi/h_i)$ wherever embedded. Penner's unrestricted decorations, understood as horocycles in the cusp cover and allowing their immersed images, form a principal $(\R_{>0})^n$-bundle. The map which assigns to $X$ the capped curve and decorations of circumferences $\ell_i(X)$ identifies its positive-length bundle with the one in Theorem \ref{A4-grafting}.

A2-collar.title: Proved: metric comparison after removing normal collars
A2-collar.statement:
\label{A2-collar}
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary and negative Euler characteristic. Remove pairwise disjoint normal collars of widths $d_i>0$ from selected boundary components, without changing the topological type, and call the remaining surface $M'$. Let $g'$ be its conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. Then $g'=e^{2u}g$ on $M'$ with $u>0$. More precisely $u$ is the unique smooth solution of
\[
\Delta_g u=e^{2u}-1\quad\hbox{on }M',\qquad
\partial_{n}u=\begin{cases}\tanh d_i&\hbox{on a new boundary},\\0&\hbox{on a retained boundary},\end{cases}
\]
where $\Delta=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{grad}$ and $n$ is the outward unit normal of $M'$. The new boundary corresponding to a former boundary of length $L_i$ has length strictly greater than $L_i\cosh d_i$ in $g'$.

A2-collar-general.title: Proved: the metric relation for every smooth collar
A2-collar-general.statement:
\label{A2-collar-general}
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary and $\chi(M)<0$. Let $M'\subset M$ be obtained by removing finitely many disjoint smooth open boundary collars, with $M'$ diffeomorphic to $M$. Write $k_g=g(\nabla_TT,n)$ on $\partial M'$, where $T$ is a unit tangent and $n$ is the outward unit normal. The unique conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary is $g'=e^{2u}g$, where $u\in C^\infty(M')$ is the unique solution
\[
 \Delta_g u=e^{2u}-1,\qquad \partial_nu=k_g.
\]
Its area and boundary lengths are exactly
\[
 \int_{M'}e^{2u}\,dA_g=-2\pi\chi(M),\qquad
 L_{g'}(B)=\int_B e^u\,ds_g\quad(B\subset\partial M').
\]
If $k_g\ge0$ everywhere and is positive somewhere, then $u>0$ everywhere. In general the sign of $u$ is not determined by the fact that a collar was removed.

A2-collar-shape.title: Proved: first variation and a family refuting general monotonicity
A2-collar-shape.statement:
\label{A2-collar-shape}
Let the boundary components of $(M,g)$ have arclength coordinates $s$, and choose smooth functions $a_i(s)>0$. In inward Fermi coordinates remove the collars
$0\le r<\varepsilon a_i(s)$, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, and let $u_\varepsilon$ be as in Theorem~\ref{A2-collar-general}. After any smooth identification with $M$ which is the identity at $\varepsilon=0$,
\[
 u_\varepsilon=\varepsilon h+O(\varepsilon^2)\quad\hbox{in }C^2,
 \qquad
 (\Delta_g-2)h=0,\quad \partial_nh=a_i-a_i''.
\]
Here the prime is differentiation in boundary arclength. In particular, take the unique hyperbolic pant all of whose boundary lengths are $2\pi$. On one boundary set
\[
 a_1(s)=1+\tfrac12\cos(ns),
\]
and on the other two set $a_2=a_3=1$. For every sufficiently large integer $n$, and then every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the resulting $u_\varepsilon$ takes a negative value at a point of the new first boundary. Thus even smooth analytic, everywhere inward collar removal need not increase the hyperbolic metric pointwise. The same metric takes a positive value somewhere.

A2-strebel-deficit.title: Proved: a uniform weighted-radius deficit
A2-strebel-deficit.statement:
\label{A2-strebel-deficit}
Put $c=2g-2+n>0$. For every $s\in(0,\infty)^I$ and every pairwise
disjoint system of pointed conformal discs $E_i$ avoiding the other
marked points,
\[
 \sum_{i\in I}s_i\bigl(\log r_i(E_i)-F_i(s)\bigr)\leq c.
\]
Consequently
\[
 0\leq K(s)-s\cdot F(s)\leq c.
\]
The constants do not depend on the boundary lengths. Fixed cusp ends
are allowed.

A2-cap-limit.title:
Proved with the stated fixed-compactification hypothesis:
the cap limit
A2-cap-limit.statement:
\label{A2-cap-limit}
Fix $Y$ and its marked points as above. Let $s^{(m)}>0$ and $t_m\to\infty$
satisfy $s^{(m)}/t_m\to p\in[0,\infty)^I\setminus\{0\}$.
For every $i$ with $p_i>0$, the pointed caps $D_i(s^{(m)})$ converge in
the Carath\'eodory kernel sense to the Jenkins--Strebel disc $U_i(p)$
with circumference weights $2\pi\sqrt{p_i}$. Their normalized conformal
maps converge locally uniformly, and
\[
 r_i(s^{(m)})\longrightarrow R_i(p).
\]
For $p_i=0$, the radii tend to zero. In particular the limit depends
on the relative growth of the lengths and on $Y$; it is not universally
a Koebe slit domain. No assertion of a fixed limit is made when the
marked compactification itself is allowed to diverge.

A2-explicit-limits.title:
Known form, with explicit derivation: the Koebe and
orange limits
A2-explicit-limits.statement:
\label{A2-explicit-limits}
Normalize a capped pant by placing its centres at $0,1,\infty$.
If $L_0\to\infty$ and $L_1/L_0,L_\infty/L_0\to0$, then the cap at
$0$ tends to $\C\setminus[1,\infty)$, its conformal radius tends to
$4$, and its normalized conformal map tends to
\[
 k(u)=\frac{4u}{(1+u)^2},\qquad |u|<1.
\]
If instead $L_0/L_1,L_0/L_\infty\to1$ and the lengths tend to infinity,
the cap at $0$ tends to
\[
 Q_0^\circ=\{|z|<1,\ \operatorname{Re}z<1/2\},
 \qquad r(Q_0,0)=\frac4{3\sqrt3}.
\]
The other two limits follow by the permutations of $0,1,\infty$.
This is the precise limiting sense in which the orange slices are valid.

A2-nonbox.title: Known inequality with derivation: the image is not a box
A2-nonbox.statement:
\label{A2-nonbox}
For the pants normalization $0,1,\infty$, every genuine admissible cap
system satisfies $r_0r_1<1$. Nevertheless the individual supremum of
each of $r_0,r_1,r_\infty$ over such systems is $4$. The set of
admissible radii is therefore not a Cartesian product of intervals.

A2b-regularity.title: Proved: regularity needed for variation
A2b-regularity.statement:
\label{A2b-regularity}
Locally in $(0,\infty)^I$, the canonical seams and their conformal cap
maps depend real-analytically on $s$. After local trivialization of each
moving piece, the hyperbolic and flat metrics depend real-analytically
on $s$. The logarithm of the metric density is $C^{1,1}$
across each seam and is smooth on either side. Its first parameter
variation is continuous across the seam and has the one-sided normal
derivatives used below.

A2b-energy.title: Proved: strict monotonicity of logarithmic cap radii
A2b-energy.statement:
\label{A2b-energy}
The Jacobian $dF/ds$ is symmetric positive definite everywhere.
Consequently $F$ is the gradient of a strictly convex real-analytic
function $S$ on $(0,\infty)^I$, and is injective. In particular an
admissible canonical cap system is determined by its conformal radii.

A2b-recession.title: Proved: uniform cap bounds and recession

A2b-image.title: Proved: exact image of the shadow map
A2b-image.statement:
\label{A2b-image}
The canonical cap radius map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism
\[
 (0,\infty)^I\longrightarrow\exp\mathcal L_Y,
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_Y=
 \left\{x\in\R^I:\ p\cdot x<K(p)
       \text{ for every }p\in[0,\infty)^I\setminus\{0\}\right\}.
\]
In particular its logarithmic image is open, convex, and downward closed.
It is precisely the set of conformal-radius vectors realized by systems
of pointed discs with pairwise disjoint analytic closures avoiding all
the other marked points. The boundary
support values are the weighted Strebel extrema \eqref{A2b-support}.

A3-boundary-chart.title: Proved: the boundary-chart exponent in 67/055--056
A3-boundary-chart.statement:
\label{A3-boundary-chart}
Let $f$ be a nonconstant holomorphic germ at zero with $f(0)=0$, real
values on the real axis, and $\operatorname{Im} f(z)\geq0$ for $z$ in
the upper half-disc. Then $f'(0)>0$. In particular the germ is locally
biholomorphic, as required by Th\'eor\`eme 1 of cote 67/055--056.

A3-rectifiable.title: Proved: the continuous-function removability of Lemma 3(c)
A3-rectifiable.statement:
\label{A3-rectifiable}
Let $U\subset\C$ be open and let $C$ be a relatively closed
rectifiable curve in $U$, or locally a finite union of rectifiable
arcs. Every continuous complex-valued function on $U$ which is
holomorphic on $U\setminus C$ is holomorphic throughout $U$.
In particular the continuous-function assertion of 67/061 is valid;
this does not by itself assert existence of a welding for an
arbitrary interval homeomorphism.

A3-welding.title: Known with proof of the form used here: circle welding
A3-welding.statement:
\label{A3-welding}
Let $X_1,X_2$ be bordered Riemann surfaces with analytic boundary, and identify selected boundary circles by orientation-reversing homeomorphisms that are quasisymmetric in analytic boundary coordinates. For finitely many such identifications, the topological quotient has a conformal structure for which the inclusions of the interiors are holomorphic and the seams are locally quasiconformal images of line segments. It is unique up to the unique conformal isomorphism restricting to the identity on every original piece. More generally, whenever a welding exists, the same uniqueness conclusion holds if its seam is conformally removable.

A3-graph.title: Proved under explicit vertex compatibility: graph welding
A3-graph.statement:
\label{A3-graph}
Theorem \ref{A3-welding} extends to finite systems of orientation-reversing boundary-arc identifications, provided that the topological quotient is an oriented surface and the identifications are quasiconformal-compatible at the vertices: in a neighborhood of each vertex there is an orientation-preserving homeomorphism to a standard finite star of sectors which is quasiconformal on each incident open sector with one common finite bound. Cutting and welding are then inverse equivalences between these marked seam surfaces and their cut surfaces with pairing data. Smooth arc identifications with compatible nonzero derivatives and finite nonzero sector angles satisfy this condition.

A3-slit.title: Known with derivation: slit uniformization and its corrected converse
A3-slit.statement:
\label{A3-slit}
Let $V$ be a Jordan domain and let $I$ be a Jordan arc joining $a\in V$ to $b\in\partial V$, with $I\setminus\{b\}\subset V$. No rectifiability is required for the conformal uniformization of the cut domain $V\setminus I$ by a disc. Its prime-end boundary consists of the outer boundary and two copies of the slit, with a single tip and two copies of its root. Specifying three positively cyclically ordered prime ends fixes the uniformizing map uniquely.

For the converse in Lemma 4B and the Scholie of 67/072--073, take the three source points $1,\zeta,\bar\zeta$, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}$, and the arcs $\beta=[1,\zeta]$, $\bar\beta=[1,\bar\zeta]$ in the source circle. Let $h:\beta\to\bar\beta$ identify the tip $1$ with itself and the two roots with each other. Assume the induced order-reversing involution on the combined arc $\beta\cup\bar\beta$ is quasisymmetric, with the endpoint compatibility of Proposition \ref{A3-graph}. Then there is a unique continuous map
\[
 f:\overline\D\to\overline\D
\]
which is conformal and injective on $\D$, has image $\D\setminus I$ there for a quasislit $I$ from $0$ to $1$, sends the source tip $1$ to $0$ and the source roots $\zeta,\bar\zeta$ to $1$, and realizes $h$ as its bank identification. Conversely, a quasiconformal image of the standard slit pair gives such pairing data. For an arbitrary slit whose welding exists, uniqueness holds whenever the slit is removable; one must not assert that every quasisymmetric welding produces a rectifiable slit.

A3-L5.title: Proved under the actual geodesic-cut hypotheses: L5
A3-L5.statement:
\label{A3-L5}
For the geodesic cutting and canonical capping operations of section 6, all boundary circle gluings are analytic diffeomorphisms. Their existence and uniqueness do not use a separate rectifiability conjecture. The same conclusion holds for smooth boundary diffeomorphisms, but mere differentiability of a homeomorphism without a nonvanishing derivative is not the same hypothesis.

A4-orange-extremal.title: Refuted, with rechecked extremal-length certificate: the orange slices
A4-orange-extremal.statement:
\label{A4-orange-extremal}
Let $Q_0=\{|z|\leq1,\ \operatorname{Re}z\leq1/2\}$ in the sphere with centres $0,1,\infty$. The canonical cap $D_0$ for a generalized pant of boundary lengths $(32,0,0)$ is not contained in $Q_0$. In particular the literal model in the letter to Bers, which permits the other two caps to degenerate to points, is false.

A4-orange-jets.title: Refuted: fixed concentric orange-slice caps
A4-orange-jets.statement:
\label{A4-orange-jets}
There are no three fixed pointed discs $Q_0,Q_1,Q_\infty$ whose independently concentric subdiscs describe all canonically capped pants. Thus the literal model in 67/019--020 is false, independently of its additional spherical description.

A4-grafting.title: Known with derivation: capping is infinite grafting
A4-grafting.statement:
\label{A4-grafting}
Let $S$ be a marked compact oriented surface of type $(g,n)$ with $n\geq1$ and negative Euler characteristic. Let $\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S)$ classify complete hyperbolic structures with each labelled end either a geodesic boundary of length $\ell_i>0$ or a cusp of length $\ell_i=0$, and with no nodes in the interior. Let $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ be its punctured Teichm\"uller space. Canonical capping gives a mapping-class-equivariant homeomorphism
\[
\Phi=(\operatorname{cap},\ell):\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S)
\longrightarrow\mathcal T_{g,n}\times[0,\infty)^n.
\]
Its restriction to each boundary-type stratum is a real-analytic diffeomorphism. In particular the positive-length part is a trivial principal $(\R_{>0})^n$-bundle over $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ by boundary lengths, not by all possible tangent radii.

A4-action.title: Proved: an intrinsic action and retraction
A4-action.statement:
\label{A4-action}
The multiplicative monoid $[0,\infty)^n$ acts continuously and intrinsically on $\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S)$ by
\[
\lambda\cdot X=\Phi^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{cap}(X),(\lambda_i\ell_i(X))_i\bigr).
\]
It commutes with the mapping class action (and with a simultaneous permutation of end labels). On the positive-length part its group of units acts freely and transitively on each capping fibre. The zero vector gives the canonical capping retraction. The maps $X\mapsto\Phi^{-1}(\operatorname{cap}(X),(1-t)\ell(X))$ give a strong deformation retraction onto the punctured locus.

A5-normalizer.title: Proved: the normalizer, including characteristic $3$ and $5$
A5-normalizer.statement:
\label{A5-normalizer}
Every faithful action of $V$ on $\mathbf P^1_k$ is conjugate to
\[
 V_0=\{z,\ -z,\ 1/z,\ -1/z\}.
\]
Its centralizer in $\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$ is $V_0$, and its normalizer is isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$. The maps
\[
 V\longmapsto N(V),\qquad \Gamma\longmapsto
 \text{the unique normal Klein subgroup of }\Gamma
\]
are inverse bijections between Klein subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$, in every characteristic different from $2$.

A5-six-points.title: Refuted in characteristic $5$; corrected proposition of 67/086
A5-six-points.statement:
\label{A5-six-points}
If $\operatorname{char}k\ne2,5$, a six-point set projectively equivalent to
$S_0=\{0,\infty,\pm1,\pm i\}$ determines a unique Klein subgroup $V$ with $S(V)=S_0$, and its full projective stabilizer is $N(V)\simeq\mathfrak S_4$.
In characteristic $5$, the same set is $\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F_5)$, its stabilizer has order $120$, and exactly five Klein subgroups have this fixed-point set. Retaining the antipodal pairing determined by $V$ restores the correspondence in characteristic $5$.

A5-faces.title: Proved: the face stabilizer correction on 67/085
A5-faces.statement:
\label{A5-faces}
A single face of the oriented octahedron has stabilizer of order $3$ in $N(V)$. An unordered pair of opposite faces has stabilizer $\mathfrak S_3$, complementary to $V$. Thus the splitting on 67/085 belongs to a pair of opposite faces.

A5-groupoid.title: Proved: the groupoid theorem of 67/089
A5-groupoid.statement:
\label{A5-groupoid}
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, and fix a choice of $i^2=-1$. Let $\mathcal C_k$ be the groupoid whose objects are projective lines $X/k$ with an embedded four-element set $I$, and whose arrows are projective isomorphisms carrying the embedded set bijectively to the embedded set. For $I$, let $J(I)$ be its three partitions into two pairs and let $Z(J(I))$ be the projective line with those three labels as marked points. Then $\mathcal C_k$ is equivalent to the groupoid of pairs
\[
 (I,\zeta),\qquad \zeta\in Z(J(I))\setminus J(I),
\]
with arrows the bijections of $I$ whose induced maps of three-pointed lines carry $\zeta$ to $\zeta'$. The torsor-twist construction on 67/088--089 is an inverse. No exception at characteristic $3$ or $5$ is needed.

A5-moduli.title: Proved with explicit distinction: L7 as a stack and as a coarse space
A5-moduli.statement:
\label{A5-moduli}
Set $R=\Z[1/2,i]$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[\lambda,\lambda^{-1},(\lambda-1)^{-1}]$. The family version of Theorem~\ref{A5-groupoid} gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{0,[4],R}\simeq[U/\mathfrak S_4],
\]
where the action factors through $\mathfrak S_4/V\simeq\mathfrak S_3$ and the usual six anharmonic transformations of $\lambda$. Its coarse moduli space is $\mathbf A^1_R$, with coordinate
\[
 J=\frac{(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3}{\lambda^2(\lambda-1)^2}.
\]
In particular the groupoid theorem does not identify the unordered moduli stack with its coarse space: generic inertia is $V$.

A2-collar-explicit.title: Proved: fixed frequency and fixed collar width
A2-collar-explicit.statement:
\label{A2-collar-explicit}
Let $M$ be the hyperbolic pant with all three geodesic boundary lengths equal to $2\pi$. Label the boundaries $B_1,B_2,B_3$, and take an arclength coordinate $s\in\R/(2\pi\Z)$ on $B_1$, with origin at its shortest perpendicular to $B_2$. Set
\[
 n=10^4,\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-14},\qquad
 a_1(s)=1+\tfrac12\cos(ns),\qquad a_2=a_3=1.
\]
In inward Fermi coordinates remove the three collars $0\le r<\varepsilon a_i(s)$. They are disjoint, everywhere inward, and have analytic boundaries. On the retained pant let $g'=e^{2u}g$ be its conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. At the point of its first boundary with $s=\pi/n$ one has
\[
 u\le-\frac{9991}{20}\,10^{-14}<0.
\]
The same function $u$ is positive somewhere. Thus the general-shape counterexample of Proposition~\ref{A2-collar-shape} can be given with these fixed parameters, without an unspecified perturbation threshold.

A1-Earle-Sipe-comparison.title: Known with derivation: the opened Earle--Sipe coordinate comparison
A1-Earle-Sipe-comparison.statement:
\label{A1-Earle-Sipe-comparison}
Let $z,w$ be disjoint local unit-disc coordinates on the two branches to be joined. For $0<r_1,r_2<1$ and $t=r_1r_2e^{i\theta}$, plumbing by $zw=t$ is precisely the analytic boundary welding which removes $|z|<r_1$ and $|w|<r_2$ and identifies
\[
 z=r_1e^{i\varphi},\qquad w=r_2e^{i(\theta-\varphi)}.
\]
Its normal tensor is $t\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w$. This is the same coordinate-level comparison as the original Earle--Sipe construction, with the full local coordinates retained.

A1-Earle-Marden-original.title: Known with derivation: identification with the opened joint Earle--Marden original
A1-Earle-Marden-original.statement:
\label{A1-Earle-Marden-original}
The joint manuscript of Earle and Marden,
\emph{Holomorphic Plumbing Coordinates on Teichm\"uller and Compactified
Moduli Space}, dated \emph{Draft 8/24/11}, gives the following identification.
It is an original author manuscript, recovered from the public archive of
Marden's Minnesota papers directory, rather than the distinct published
2012 chapter. The relevant locators are \S4.1.1--4.1.2, pp.~39--40;
\S4.5, p.~50; and \S4.8.1--4.8.2, equations~(4.8.1)--(4.8.2),
p.~57 \cite{EarleMarden2011DraftA567}.

Normalize the peripheral translation to $A(\zeta)=\zeta+1$.
Suppose the two disjoint puncture neighborhoods are the quotients of
$\operatorname{Im}\zeta>h$ and $\operatorname{Im}\eta<-h$, where $h>0$.
For $\tau=a+2si$, $s>h$, the identification
$\zeta=\eta+\tau$ becomes classical plumbing
\[
 z=e^{2\pi i\zeta},\qquad w=e^{-2\pi i\eta},\qquad
 zw=t,\qquad t=e^{2\pi i\tau}.
\]
Writing $\rho=e^{-2\pi h}$ and $r=e^{-2\pi s}$ gives the exact bounds
\[
 0<r<\rho<1,\qquad |t|=r^2<\rho^2=e^{-4\pi h}.
\]
The sewn collar is the annulus
\[
 \frac{|t|}{\rho}<|z|<\rho,\qquad
 \operatorname{mod}=\frac{1}{2\pi}\log\frac{\rho^2}{|t|}
                   =\operatorname{Im}\tau-2h.
\]
On its middle circle the sewing is
$re^{i\theta}\mapsto re^{i(\phi-\theta)}$, where
$t=|t|e^{i\phi}$. More generally, after rescaling by positive
$0<r_+,r_-<\rho$ satisfying $r_+r_-=|t|$, put $u=z/r_+$ and $v=w/r_-$.
Then the same sewing is
\[
 uv=e^{i\phi},\qquad
 t\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w
   =e^{i\phi}\,\partial_u\otimes\partial_v.
\]
Thus the toric boundary welding in Proposition~\ref{A1-welding-plumbing}
is exactly this plumbing operation when its full coordinate germs are
retained. The normal tensor is its first-order invariant.

A6-intrinsic-tame.title: Proved: an intrinsic tame Galois category
A6-intrinsic-tame.statement:
\label{A6-intrinsic-tame}
Let $R$ be a complete noetherian discrete valuation ring, let
$F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ have characteristic zero, and let $U/F$ be
nonempty, smooth, geometrically connected, separated and of finite type.
A test trait is a discrete valuation ring $A$, not a field, with an
$R$-algebra structure, together with an $R$-morphism
\[
 f_A:\eta_A=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(A)\longrightarrow U.
\]
The ring $A$ need not be excellent, henselian, or of finite type over
$R$; the structure map need not be local. In particular, tests for
which a uniformizer of $R$ becomes a unit in $A$ are included.
Give $T_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the divisorial log structure of its
closed point, denoted $T_A^{\log}$.

Define $\operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ to be the full subcategory
of $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ consisting of covers $V\to U$ such
that, for every test trait, $f_A^*V\to\eta_A$ is the generic fibre of
a \emph{finite Kummer-\'etale cover} of $T_A^{\log}$.
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item With the restriction of any geometric fibre functor on $U$,
 $\operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ is a Galois category. It is closed
 in $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ under finite limits, finite sums,
 subobjects and quotients. Its fundamental group
 $\Pi^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ is a quotient of $\pi_1(U)$.
\item Pullback along an $F$-morphism $U'\to U$ between such varieties
 preserves these categories. Pullback of tame covers of
 $\operatorname{Spec}R$ gives a natural surjection
 $\Pi^{\rm tr}_R(U)\twoheadrightarrow G_F^t$.
\item Whenever a proper integral noetherian fs log-regular model
 $\mathcal X^{\log}\to(\operatorname{Spec}R)^{\log}$ with interior
 $U$ exists, one has equality of full subcategories
 \[
  \operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U)
     =\operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U)
       \subseteq\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U).
 \]
 Consequently the equivalence with finite Kummer-\'etale covers of
 the strict special log fibre in
 Theorem~\ref{A6-tame-specialization} realizes this intrinsic category.
\end{enumerate}

A1-pant-third-jet.title: Proved: the third jet of a one-active-cap pant
A1-pant-third-jet.statement:
\label{A1-pant-third-jet}
Let the hyperbolic pant have one boundary of length $2\pi\lambda$,
$\lambda>0$, and two cusps. Normalize its capped sphere by placing
the cap centre at $0$ and the ordered cusps at $1,\infty$.
Let $r(\lambda)$ be the cap's conformal radius, and normalize its
unit-disc coordinate $u_\lambda$ to have positive derivative at
zero. Then
\[
 g_\lambda(z):=r(\lambda)u_\lambda(z)
       =z+\frac12z^2+\beta(\lambda)z^3+O(z^4),
 \qquad
 \beta(\lambda)=\frac5{16}
                 +\frac1{16(\lambda^2+4)}.
\]
Moreover $r:(0,\infty)\to(0,4)$ is a strictly increasing
real-analytic bijection.

A1-four-point-plumbing-jet.title: Proved: a four-point plumbing coefficient
A1-four-point-plumbing-jet.statement:
\label{A1-four-point-plumbing-jet}
On two spheres with node $0$ and external markings $1,\infty$,
take node-coordinate germs
\[
 g_i(z)=z+\frac12z^2+\beta_i z^3+O(z^4),\qquad i=1,2.
\]
Plumb by $g_1(z)g_2(w)=t$. On the resulting four-pointed sphere,
normalize the global coordinate so that the first component's
$\infty$ is $\infty$, its $1$ is $1$, and the second component's
$\infty$ is $0$. Let $\Lambda(t)$ be the coordinate of the second
component's $1$. Then
\[
 \Lambda(t)=t-\frac12t^2+
 \left(\frac9{16}-\frac54(\beta_1+\beta_2)
                         +4\beta_1\beta_2\right)t^3+O(t^4).
\]
In particular, for the germs of Lemma~\ref{A1-pant-third-jet},
the cubic coefficient is
\[
 C(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)
   =\frac{11}{64}
       +\frac1{64(\lambda_1^2+4)(\lambda_2^2+4)}.
\]

A1-toric-nondescent.title: Refuted: raw toric surgery is invariant under isotopy in a fixed surface
A1-toric-nondescent.statement:
\label{A1-toric-nondescent}
There is a four-labelled punctured sphere $X$ with two isotopic
essential analytic cuts $C,C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ such that both cuts
are canonically torically compatible, $C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is the
unique hyperbolic geodesic in their isotopy class, and raw canonical
cutting and capping produces different nodal tensors. Thus raw
toric surgery does not descend to a functor on cut isotopy classes.
Replacing a representative by its geodesic before applying surgery
defines the different, well-defined functor already studied.

A1-toric-domain.title: Proved: the broader toric domain, its exact image, and its extra fibers
A1-toric-domain.statement:
\label{A1-toric-domain}
The tensor and external-shadow map from $\mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$
has exactly the same image $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ as the
equal-length geodesic map of
Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}; for $L=\varnothing$ this is
$\mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)$ of Theorem~\ref{A1-graph-range}. In particular
\[
 P_*(D_Y)=\left\{y:\ p\cdot y<K_{\Gamma,L}(p)
                   \text{ for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\right\}.
\]
This is a proper subset of the unrestricted tensor/shadow fiber
whenever $P\ne\varnothing$; when $P=\varnothing$ it is the
entire one-point fiber.
Before finite automorphism quotients, the fiber over a fixed tensor
and shadow tuple is an open convex set of dimension $|E|$ in its
full cap logarithms. More strongly, after orienting each edge, the
quantities
\[
 d_e=s_{h_e^+}-s_{h_e^-}\in\R
\]
give a global real-analytic identification
\[
 \mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y)
       \simeq\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)\times\R^E,
\]
under which the surgery map is projection and the geodesic submodel
is $d=0$. Thus its tangent map is surjective with kernel dimension
$|E|$; it is an isomorphism precisely when $E=\varnothing$.
If the normalization varies and the graph has total genus $g$ and
$n$ external markings, the broader toric source has real dimension
$6g-6+2n+|L|+|E|$, whereas the tensor/shadow target has dimension
$6g-6+2n+|L|$. Thus the dimension count in 67/077 applies to the
geodesic model, not to actual toric cuts of independent lengths.

The identification is intrinsic if $\R^E$ is regarded as the real
space of antisymmetric functions on the two branches of each edge.
Branch interchange changes the corresponding $d_e$ to $-d_e$,
and graph automorphisms also permute edges. The construction varies
real-analytically with the normalization and is equivariant.
Consequently it defines a real vector orbibundle over the geodesic
image when finite automorphisms are retained. Scaling $d$ to zero
is a fiber-preserving equivariant strong deformation retraction.
The broader toric surgery map therefore induces the same
fundamental-group isomorphism to the unrestricted tensor/shadow
target, although its tangent map has a nonzero kernel whenever
there is a cut.

A1-toric-noninjective.title: Refuted: toric compatibility alone implies an inverse
A1-toric-noninjective.statement:
\label{A1-toric-noninjective}
Even for the unbordered four-labelled sphere with one separating
analytic cut, the torically compatible surgery map is not
injective. There are distinct such cut objects with fixed
normalization and tensor $q=\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_w|_0$.

A1-toric-full-discs.title: Proved: what changes when full external discs are retained
A1-toric-full-discs.statement:
\label{A1-toric-full-discs}
For the broader toric interpretation, retain arbitrary pointed
external discs with disjoint analytic closures, in addition to
the tensors. Such a tuple $(Y,q,(D_l))$ is a surgery output if and
only if its external shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ and tensors belong to
$\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ and there exists $d\in\R^E$ for which
the unique canonical cap system constructed in
Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain} has external members exactly $D_l$.
Its fiber is precisely this set of $d$'s, with the prescribed
finite automorphism identifications. In particular the
$\R^E$-fiber assertion concerns the tensor/shadow target; it
must not be transferred to a target retaining full external
disc shapes. The geodesic criterion of
Corollary~\ref{A1-bordered-shape-image} is the special case $d=0$.

A6-ordinary-counterexample.title: Refuted for the ordinary fundamental group
A6-ordinary-counterexample.statement:
\label{A6-ordinary-counterexample}
The ordinary arithmetic fundamental group of a stable marked curve cannot reconstruct a chosen nonzero normal tensor, even for $(g,n)=(0,4)$ over $\Q$. Moreover its geometric version does not retain nodal inertia.

A6-kummer.title: Proved: Kummer separation for the fields on 049
A6-kummer.statement:
\label{A6-kummer}
For a field $K$ finitely generated over $\Q$, the Kummer map
\[
 K^\times\longrightarrow H^1(G_K,\widehat{\Z}(1))
\]
is injective. Also $(\widehat{\Z}(1))^{G_K}=0$.

A6-graphic.title: Known with derivation: graphical fullness over a finitely generated field

A6-normal-kummer.title: Known with explicit comparison: normal tensors and twists
A6-normal-kummer.statement:
\label{A6-normal-kummer}
Fix a stable marked curve $Y/K$ as above. After a finite extension splitting its nodes and branches, choose bases for their normal lines. For two propagators $N=(c_e)$ and $N'=(c'_e)$, geometric transport identifies their admissible groups, and the difference of their arithmetic outer actions is the cocycle
\[
 \bigl(\kappa(c'_e/c_e)\bigr)_e
 \ \in Z^1\!\left(G_K,\prod_e\widehat{\Z}(1)\right).
\]
Changing that transport changes the cocycle by a coboundary. The group of graphic automorphisms that act identically on the underlying graph and on every component anabelioid is precisely the displayed product of profinite Dehn twist groups. This statement includes loops and self-nodes.

A6-anabelian.title: Proved under the specified logarithmic interpretation: 049(a)
A6-anabelian.statement:
\label{A6-anabelian}
Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, and let $(Y,N)$ and $(Y',N')$ be geometrically connected stable marked curves with nonzero normal tensors as above. For the framed logarithmic fundamental groups, the natural map
\[
 \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((Y,N),(Y',N')\bigr)
 \longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K}
       \bigl(\Delta_{Y,N},\Delta_{Y',N'}\bigr)
\]
is bijective. Labels, if prescribed, must be preserved on both sides. In particular, the graph, component curves, marked points, and actual normal tensors are all recovered. The use of a framed logarithmic group is a hypothesis of this theorem and is the interpretation needed for the manuscript's normal propagator.

A6-procyclic.title: Refuted as a bare criterion; corrected recovery in 049(b)
A6-procyclic.statement:
\label{A6-procyclic}
The condition of being isomorphic to $\widehat{\Z}$, with invariant conjugacy class and cyclotomic arithmetic action, does not put such subgroups in bijection with nodes and marked points. Even with all points rational, infinitely many subgroups satisfy it. The strongest reconstruction statement established here is instead the canonical recovery of the full finite graph and all its maximal node and cusp inertia groups in Lemma~\ref{A6-graphic}. It uses the arithmetic action on finite covers, not merely the proposed condition on an individual subgroup.

A6-cyclotomic-detection.title: Known: the precise smooth-curve cyclotomic criterion
A6-cyclotomic-detection.statement:
\label{A6-cyclotomic-detection}
Let $U/k$ be a smooth affine geometrically connected hyperbolic curve
over a number field, with $\Pi=\pi_1(U)$ and geometric kernel $\Delta$.
For $1\ne z\in\Delta$, the element $z$ belongs to a conjugate of a cusp
inertia group if and only if there is a closed subgroup $N\subset\Pi$
whose image in $G_k$ is open and such that
\[
 nzn^{-1}=z^{\chi(n)}\qquad(n\in N).
\]
Here $\chi$ is the cyclotomic character pulled back from $G_k$.

A6-three-classes.title: Refuted literally; clarified geometric reading of NB 048
A6-three-classes.statement:
\label{A6-three-classes}
For every hyperbolic type $(g,n)$ in characteristic zero, there are infinitely many conjugacy classes of injective continuous homomorphisms $\widehat{\Z}(1)\to\Delta_{g,n}$. Thus the NB cannot literally assert that there are three such classes, or two when $n=0$.

For geometric simple loops there is a meaningful three-way division into peripheral, separating essential, and nonseparating loops. This is a division into kinds, not three conjugacy classes. Under the mapping class group with unordered punctures, peripheral loops have one orbit when $n>0$, nonseparating loops one orbit when $g>0$, and separating loops have orbits indexed by unordered admissible pairs
\[
 \{(h,r),(g-h,n-r)\},\qquad
 2h+r-1>0,\quad 2(g-h)+(n-r)-1>0.
\]
For labelled punctures their subsets must also be specified.

A6-blowup.title: Proved: the unadorned fundamental group cannot select a compactification
A6-blowup.statement:
\label{A6-blowup}
Let $U=(\mathbf P^1_\Q\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. The same smooth variety, and hence the same augmented arithmetic fundamental group, admits two nonisomorphic smooth proper compactifications with strict normal-crossings boundary, containing respectively six and seven irreducible boundary components.

A6-SNC-existence.title: Known with derivation: existence in arbitrary dimension
A6-SNC-existence.statement:
\label{A6-SNC-existence}
Every smooth separated finite-type variety over a characteristic-zero field has a smooth proper compactification with reduced strict normal-crossings boundary. Therefore every member of $\mathcal A$ has a tangential log compactification in the stated sense.

A6-log-specialization.title: Known with derivation: logarithmic tangential specialization
A6-log-specialization.statement:
\label{A6-log-specialization}
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, $R=k[[t]]$, $F=k((t))$, and let $S^{\log}$ be $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the divisorial log structure of $t=0$. Let $\mathcal X^{\log}\to S^{\log}$ be a proper morphism of noetherian fs log schemes with $\mathcal X^{\log}$ log regular. Suppose its interior $U$ is contained in the generic fibre and is geometrically connected over $F$. Put
\[
 X_0^{\log}=\mathcal X^{\log}\times_{S^{\log}}s^{\log},
\]
where $s^{\log}$ is the strict closed log point. Restriction gives equivalences
\[
 \operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log})
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(X_0^{\log}).
\]
Consequently there is an outer isomorphism
\[
 \pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U)\simeq
 \pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(X_0^{\log})
 \quad\hbox{over}\quad
 G_F\simeq\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log}).
\]
The frame $t$ gives a section
$\sigma_t:G_k\to\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log})
\simeq\widehat{\Z}(1)\rtimes G_k$. Pullback along that section defines a tangential specialization extension
\[
 1\longrightarrow\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_{\overline{F}})
 \longrightarrow
 \pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(X_0^{\log})
       \times_{\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log})}G_k
 \longrightarrow G_k\longrightarrow1.
\]
In particular this applies to proper log-smooth saturated semistable pairs, with horizontal boundary included. It retains the logarithmic special fibre, rather than replacing it by the ordinary singular fibre.

A6-canonical-compactification.title: Proved: reconstruction of a log-canonically polarized compactification
A6-canonical-compactification.statement:
\label{A6-canonical-compactification}
Let $(X,D)$ and $(X',D')$ be smooth proper pairs over a characteristic-zero field $k$, with reduced strict normal-crossings boundaries. Suppose
$L=\omega_X(D)$ and $L'=\omega_{X'}(D')$ are ample. Every isomorphism
$U=X\setminus D\simeq X'\setminus D'=U'$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism of pairs.

Consequently, on any isomorphism-anabelian class $\mathcal A$, the map
\[
 \operatorname{Isom}_k((X,D),(X',D'))
 \longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Isom}_{G_k}
       \bigl(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U),\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U')\bigr)
       /\operatorname{Inn}\bigl(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U'_{\overline{k}})\bigr)
\]
is bijective for these compactifications. In particular their strata, normal-torus diagrams and the associated tangential fibre functors are recovered functorially.

A6-matrix-presentations.title: Proved: the two matrix presentations on 050
A6-matrix-presentations.statement:
\label{A6-matrix-presentations}
The presentations, with the involution relations made explicit, are
\[
 \operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)
 =\langle \sigma,\rho\mid \sigma^2=\rho^3,\ \rho^6=1\rangle,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)
 =\langle r_1,r_2,r_3\mid
 r_1^2=r_2^2=r_3^2=1,\
 (r_1r_2)^2=(r_2r_3)^3,\
 (r_1r_2)^4=1\rangle.
\]
We may take
\[
 \sigma=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 \rho=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 r_1=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\
 r_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\
 r_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In particular these identify the ordinary and extended once-punctured torus groups.

A6-four-punctures.title: Proved: the four-punctured sphere and both superscript readings
A6-four-punctures.statement:
\label{A6-four-punctures}
For the four-punctured sphere,
\[
 \operatorname{PMod}(S_{0,4})\simeq F_2
 \simeq \Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Mod}(S_{0,4})
 \simeq V_4\rtimes\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z).
\]
The subgroup fixing one specified puncture is $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)$, and the quotient of the full group by its displayed normal $V_4$ is also $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)$. Thus the formula with $+!$ is false if that symbol consistently means the pure group; it is correct if the second superscript means the distinguished-point subgroup. The exact diagram intended by the main part of 051 is
\[
 \begin{array}{ccccccccc}
 1&\longrightarrow&F_2&\longrightarrow&
 \operatorname{Mod}(S_{0,4})&\longrightarrow&S_4&\longrightarrow&1\\
 &&\Vert&&\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
 1&\longrightarrow&\Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\}&\longrightarrow&
 \operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)&\longrightarrow&S_3&\longrightarrow&1 .
 \end{array}
\]

A6-binary-S3.title: Proved: a consistent reading of the partly erased lift on 051
A6-binary-S3.statement:
\label{A6-binary-S3}
There is an exact sequence
\[
 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)
 \longrightarrow\widetilde{S}_3\longrightarrow1,
\]
where $\widetilde{S}_3$ is the binary dihedral group of order $12$. It can be obtained as a quotient of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z/4\Z)$, as suggested by the partially erased formula on the sheet. The quotient by $\{\pm I\}$ gives the lower row of Proposition~\ref{A6-four-punctures}. This is not the ordinary reduction-modulo-$2$ sequence, whose kernel contains $-I$.

A6-projective-line.title: Proved: the integral projective-line quotient on 051
A6-projective-line.statement:
\label{A6-projective-line}
With
\[
 B_\infty=\left\{\ \pm\begin{pmatrix}1&n\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
                    :n\in\Z\right\},
\]
there are bijections of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)$-sets
\[
 \operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)/B_\infty
 \simeq\mathbf P^1(\Z)\simeq\mathbf P^1(\Q).
\]
Reduction gives the displayed surjection
$\mathbf P^1(\Z)\to\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F_2)$.
These are point sets; the quotient written on the sheet is not an identification with the entire scheme $\mathbf P^1_{\Z}$.

A6-birman.title: Known with the missing hypotheses: the Birman sequence
A6-birman.statement:
\label{A6-birman}
Let $S=S_{g,n-1}$ be an oriented surface with $2g-2+(n-1)>0$, and let $p$ be an additional marked point. There are exact sequences
\[
 1\longrightarrow\pi_1(S,p)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Mod}(S,p)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(S)
 \longrightarrow1,
\]
and their pure and extended versions. Here the middle group fixes $p$; forgetting one point is not a map from a group that is allowed to interchange that point with all the others. The same form holds with boundary fixed pointwise. The positivity condition is essential.

A6-presentation-types.title: Known with derivation: pants, Lego, and involutions
A6-presentation-types.statement:
\label{A6-presentation-types}
The three presentation mechanisms anticipated on 050 have rigorous realizations, with different conventions. The pants and Lego mechanisms give complete mapping-class \emph{groupoid} presentations by local moves and their relations. Closed extended mapping class groups of every genus $g\ge1$ admit finite presentations on orientation-reversing involutions; generation by three such involutions is known. These assertions do not by themselves identify an arithmetic automorphism group of the full Teichm\"uller tower.

A6-model-system.title: Proved: the canonical system of smooth compactifications
A6-model-system.statement:
\label{A6-model-system}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $U/k$ be smooth,
geometrically connected, separated and of finite type. Define
$\mathcal C_k(U)$ as follows. An object is a smooth proper integral
$k$-scheme $X$, with a specified dense open immersion $j_X:U\hookrightarrow X$
whose reduced complement $D_X$ is a strict normal-crossings divisor.
A morphism from $X$ to $Y$ is a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ satisfying
$f\circ j_X=j_Y$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\mathcal C_k(U)$ is essentially small, nonempty and cofiltered.
There is at most one morphism between any two objects. Every morphism
is proper and satisfies $f^{-1}(j_Y(U))=j_X(U)$.
\item Its inverse system, with its marked common interior,
\[
 \mathfrak C_k(U)=\bigl((X,D_X)\bigr)_{X\in\mathcal C_k(U)},
 \qquad U\longrightarrow\mathfrak C_k(U),
\]
is independent, up to canonical pro-isomorphism, of the choice of a
small skeleton. For any fixed model $X_0$, restricting to all models
dominating $X_0$ gives the same pro-object. The same holds after fixing
any finite collection of initial models.
\item Every $k$-isomorphism $\varphi:U\to V$ extends uniquely to an
isomorphism of these pro-systems with their marked interiors. Thus,
on any class $\mathcal A$ for which the augmented arithmetic fundamental
group is fully faithful on isomorphisms, that group reconstructs
$\mathfrak C_k(U)$ functorially. The reconstructed object retains the
schemes, boundaries and transition maps, not just the abstract indexing
partially ordered set.
\end{enumerate}
Here an isomorphism of marked pro-systems includes the isomorphism of
their interiors and commutes with the displayed maps from those
interiors. The theorem makes no selection of one compactification.

A6-model-specialization.title: Proved: compatibility of tangential specialization across models
A6-model-specialization.statement:
\label{A6-model-specialization}
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, put $R=k[[t]]$ and $F=k((t))$, and fix
a smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type $F$-scheme $U$.
Consider proper integral regular $R$-schemes $\mathcal X$ containing
$U$ as a dense open, with reduced complement $D_{\mathcal X}$ a strict
normal-crossings divisor. Give them their divisorial log structures,
and give $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the log structure of $t=0$.
Their morphisms are $R$-morphisms restricting to $\operatorname{id}_U$.
This category is nonempty and cofiltered. Every such model is flat
over $R$, and it has a canonical morphism of log schemes to $S^{\log}$.

For every model, write $\mathcal X_0^{\log}$ for its strict closed
log fibre. The equivalences
\[
 \operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log})
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log})
\]
are compatible with every transition map. In particular, if
$f:\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$ is one, then
\[
 f_0^*:\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log})
       \longrightarrow
       \operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0'{}^{\log})
\]
is an equivalence. The comparisons between any two models are independent
of common refinement, up to the unique natural isomorphism compatible
with restriction to $U$. They preserve the maps to $G_F$ and, for the
same chosen frame $t$, the tangential specialization extensions over
$G_k$ of Theorem~\ref{A6-log-specialization}.

A6-special-fibre-counterexample.title: Refuted: reconstruction of a chosen special fibre
A6-special-fibre-counterexample.statement:
\label{A6-special-fibre-counterexample}
Over $R=\Q[[t]]$, there are two proper integral regular models of the
same smooth geometrically connected generic open, both with strict
normal-crossings reduced boundary, whose special fibres are not
isomorphic. Nevertheless their strict special log fibres have equivalent
finite Kummer-\'etale cover categories over $G_{\Q((t))}$ and the same
tangential arithmetic extension over $G_\Q$ for the fixed frame $t$.
Thus even these augmented and framed cover data do not reconstruct a
chosen special-fibre scheme. This does not contradict reconstruction of
the complete marked model system.

A6-tame-specialization.title:
Known comparison with proved model independence:
 mixed-characteristic tame specialization
A6-tame-specialization.statement:
\label{A6-tame-specialization}
Let $R$ be a complete noetherian discrete valuation ring, with fraction
field $F$ of characteristic zero and residue field $k$ of characteristic
$p\geq0$. Give $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the divisorial log structure of
its closed point. Let $U/F$ be a smooth geometrically connected
separated finite-type variety.
Suppose that $\mathcal X^{\log}\to S^{\log}$ is a proper morphism of
noetherian fs log schemes, that $\mathcal X^{\log}$ is integral and log
regular, and that its interior is identified with $U$. Write
$\mathcal X_0^{\log}$ for its strict closed log fibre. Then restriction
gives equivalences
\[
 \operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U)
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log})
 \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log}).
\]
They commute with pullback from $S^{\log}$.

If $\mathcal Y^{\log}$ is any other model satisfying these same
hypotheses for the same $U$ and $R$, then
\[
 \operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U)
       =\operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal Y}(U)
       \quad\text{as full subcategories of }\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U).
\]
Consequently the special-log-fibre cover categories are canonically
equivalent through this common category. The comparisons are independent
of a common refinement, whose existence is not assumed. They are unique
up to the natural isomorphism normalized by their restriction to $U$.
For an actual log morphism of models fixing $U$, its pullback is this
equivalence.

Let $G_F^t$ be the quotient of $G_F$ classifying finite extensions tame
over $R$, and let $\Pi^t(U)$ be the fundamental group of the common
tame-cover category. There is a natural surjection
$\Pi^t(U)\to G_F^t$. A uniformizer $\varpi$ supplies a section
\[
 \sigma_{\varpi}:G_k\longrightarrow G_F^t,
 \qquad
 G_F^t\simeq\widehat{\Z}^{(p')}(1)\rtimes G_k,
\]
where all primes are retained when $p=0$. If
$\Delta^t=\ker(\Pi^t(U)\to G_F^t)$, the resulting tangential extension
\[
 1\longrightarrow\Delta^t\longrightarrow
 \Pi^t(U)\times_{G_F^t}G_k
 \longrightarrow G_k\longrightarrow1
\]
is independent of the chosen model. For $p>0$ we do not identify
$\Delta^t$ with the full geometric \'etale fundamental group, nor do
we replace $G_F^t$ by $G_F$.

A6-frobenius-counterexample.title:
Refuted: preservation of the strict Isom-anabelian
 definition under reduction
A6-frobenius-counterexample.statement:
\label{A6-frobenius-counterexample}
The characteristic-zero Isom-anabelian property used in the
compactification definition is not preserved unchanged under arithmetic
specialization. There are two nonisomorphic hyperbolic curves over
$k=\mathbf F_{16}$ whose augmented \'etale fundamental groups are
isomorphic over $G_k$. Both are good reductions of hyperbolic curves
over the number field $\Q(\zeta_{15})$.

A6-wild-counterexample.title:
Refuted: replacing tame covers by all covers in
 mixed characteristic
A6-wild-counterexample.statement:
\label{A6-wild-counterexample}
The first equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A6-tame-specialization} is false
with $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ in place of the tame subcategory,
even for a smooth proper relative curve with strict normal-crossings
boundary and hyperbolic generic interior.

A6-node-character.title:
Refuted without split branches; exact corrected
 inertia character
A6-node-character.statement:
\label{A6-node-character}
Let $e$ be a geometric node of a stable curve in the framed logarithmic
interpretation of Theorem~\ref{A6-anabelian}, over a characteristic-zero
field $K$. On the subgroup of $G_K$ stabilizing $e$, let
$\varepsilon_e$ be the character which is $1$ when the two branches
are preserved and $-1$ when they are interchanged. The character on
its node inertia group is
\[
 I_e\simeq\widehat{\Z}(1)\otimes\varepsilon_e,
 \qquad \gamma\longmapsto\chi_{\rm cyc}(\gamma)\varepsilon_e(\gamma).
\]
In particular the invariant-conjugacy-class condition does not by
itself make the character cyclotomic. It becomes cyclotomic after
passing to the branch-splitting field. Marked-point inertia has the
ordinary cyclotomic character on its point stabilizer.

A7-gluing-modules.title: Proved: the categorical statement of 67/091
A7-gluing-modules.statement:
\label{A7-gluing-modules}
Let $R$ be a ring, not necessarily commutative, and use left $R$-modules. The category of pairs $(M,\sigma)$ with $M$ an $R$-module, multiplication by $2$ injective on $M$, and $\sigma^2=1$, is equivalent to the category of triples $(P,Q,m)$, where $P,Q$ are $2$-torsion-free $R$-modules and
\[
 m\subset(P/2P)\oplus(Q/2Q),\qquad
 m\cap(P/2P)=m\cap(Q/2Q)=0.
\]
Morphisms of triples are pairs of module maps preserving $m$ after reduction modulo $2$. No Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis is required. In the proof, localization at $2$ is valid because the integer $2$ is central; equivalently, $M[1/2]=M\otimes_{\Z}\Z[1/2]$.

A7-domain-counterexample.title: Refuted: connectedness does not repair the line-bundle corollary
A7-domain-counterexample.statement:
\label{A7-domain-counterexample}
The assertion following 67/091 that the two eigenspaces of a nontrivial involution on a rank-two projective module are invertible is false even over a $2$-torsion-free domain. Thus the supplied correction ``needs $\operatorname{Spec}R$ connected (e.g. a domain)'' is insufficient.
A counterexample is
\[
 R=\Z[x,y,z]/(x^2+yz-1),\qquad M=R^2,
 \qquad \sigma=\begin{pmatrix}x&y\\z&-x\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The categorical statement in Proposition~\ref{A7-gluing-modules} remains valid. Its eigenspaces are invertible under either of the sufficient hypotheses: $R$ is a Dedekind domain and $M$ is finite projective of rank two; or $2$ is invertible in $R$, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is connected, and $M$ is finite projective of rank two. In these two cases we require $\sigma\ne\pm1$.

A7-PID-count.title: Proved: the exact count in 67/100
A7-PID-count.statement:
\label{A7-PID-count}
Suppose $R$ is a PID, $2\ne0$, and $\kappa=R/2R$ is a field. Conjugacy classes of involutions $\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_2(R)$ with $\sigma\ne\pm1$ consist of one split class and a set of nonsplit classes canonically indexed by
\[
 \kappa^\times/\operatorname{im}(R^\times\to\kappa^\times).
\]
For $R=\Z$ there are two classes in total. For
$R=\Z[(1+\sqrt{-11})/2]$ there are four classes in total, three of them nonsplit. The struck surjectivity proviso on 67/100 is therefore necessary for the assertion that there is just one nonsplit class.

A7-real-classification.title: Known with complete derivation: classification on 67/093--099
A7-real-classification.statement:
\label{A7-real-classification}
For $a>0$ define real elliptic curves by their complex uniformizations and the indicated conjugation:
\[
 E_a:\quad \C/(\Z+i\sqrt a\,\Z),\qquad
 E'_a:\quad \C/\bigl(\Z+\tfrac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\Z\bigr),
 \qquad \sigma[z]=[\bar{z}].
\]
These two disjoint families, with the parameter $a$ unique in each, are the complete list of origin-marked real elliptic curves up to real isomorphism. Their real origin-preserving automorphism groups are $\{\pm1\}$.

A fixed complex elliptic curve has real forms if and only if its usual modular invariant $j$ is real, and then has exactly two real isomorphism classes. Outside the square case they are either $\{E_a,E_{1/a}\}$ or $\{E'_a,E'_{1/a}\}$ with $a>1$. For the square lattice they are $\{E_1,E'_1\}$. For the hexagonal lattice they are $\{E'_3,E'_{1/3}\}$.

A7-ratio-j.title: Refuted: the numerical guesses on 67/097--098
A7-ratio-j.statement:
\label{A7-ratio-j}
With $Q$ the quadratic form used on 67/093 and 099, the hexagonal ratio is $3$, not $\sqrt3$. The usual modular invariant is
\[
 j(E_a)=j(i\sqrt a),\qquad
 j(E'_a)=j\left(\frac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\right),
\]
and is unchanged by $a\mapsto1/a$ in either family. It is not $c\log a$ for either tentative nonzero constant in 67/097.

A7-real-topology.title: Proved: real points, torsors, and the topology on 67/101

thm:B1a-betti.title: Proved; L1 over the complex numbers
thm:B1a-betti.statement:
\label{thm:B1a-betti}
Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex variety of dimension four.
Two codimension-two cycles with rational coefficients on $X$ are numerically
equivalent if and only if their rational Betti classes agree.

lem:B-basechange-num.title: Proved; numerical triviality and field extension
lem:B-basechange-num.statement:
\label{lem:B-basechange-num}
Let $X/k$ be smooth projective, $K/k$ a field extension, and
$z\in\mathrm{CH}^r(X)_{\Q}$. Then $z$ is numerically trivial if and only if
$z_K$ is numerically trivial.

thm:B1a-etale.title: Proved; B.1(a) and L1 over every characteristic-zero field
thm:B1a-etale.statement:
\label{thm:B1a-etale}
Let $k$ be any field of characteristic zero, $X/k$ smooth projective of
pure dimension four, and $\ell$ any prime. Numerical and geometric
$\ell$-adic homological equivalence coincide for codimension-two cycles
with rational coefficients on $X$.

prop:B1b-criterion.title: Proved; the precise positivity criterion
prop:B1b-criterion.statement:
\label{prop:B1b-criterion}
Fix a Weil cohomology on smooth projective varieties over a field $k$.
Let $X/k$ be a smooth projective fourfold and $h$ an ample divisor class.
Suppose that its algebraic classes in $H^4$ admit the orthogonal
decomposition
\[
 A^2=\Q h^2\oplus hA^1_{\mathrm{prim}}\oplus A^2_{\mathrm{prim}},
\]
that the intersection form is negative definite on
$hA^1_{\mathrm{prim}}$ and positive definite on
$A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}$. Positivity here is on the $\Q$-vector spaces of
\emph{homological} algebraic classes, before dividing by numerical
equivalence. Then numerical and homological equivalence coincide in
codimension two. Conversely, if the decomposition exists, numerical
primitive positivity together with numerical--homological equality
implies this criterion.

prop:B1b-gap.title: Proved; limitation of the proposed Ancona-only inference
prop:B1b-gap.statement:
\label{prop:B1b-gap}
The Lefschetz standard conjecture and positivity of the primitive form
\emph{on numerical classes} do not, by the preceding linear-algebra
argument alone, prove numerical--homological equality. Ancona's 2021
theorem supplies this numerical positivity for abelian fourfolds; its
stated equality theorem covers infinitely many primes $\ell$, not every
$\ell$.

thm:B1b-abelian.title: Known with checked deduction from a 2026 preprint; B.1(b)
thm:B1b-abelian.statement:
\label{thm:B1b-abelian}
Let $A/k$ be an abelian fourfold over any field and let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Numerical and $\ell$-adic homological
equivalence coincide for all cycles on $A$ with rational coefficients,
in particular for its two-dimensional cycles.

prop:B1b-scope.title: Proved under stated hypotheses; scope of the same argument
prop:B1b-scope.statement:
\label{prop:B1b-scope}
The positivity-and-specialization argument applies to every smooth
projective fourfold $X/k$ whose algebraic Lefschetz decomposition exists
and which has a smooth projective specialization $X_0$ for which
numerical--$\ell$-adic equality and numerical primitive positivity both
hold. It also proves numerical--$\ell$-adic equality on every smooth
projective fourfold dominated by a smooth projective fourfold $Y$ having
that equality, by a generically finite surjective morphism
$f:Y\to X$. In particular it applies to fourfolds dominated in this
sense by an abelian fourfold.

thm:B1c.title: Refuted; numerically trivial curves need not be $\tau$-trivial
thm:B1c.statement:
\label{thm:B1c}
With the classical definition of $\tau$-triviality (some nonzero integral multiple is
algebraically equivalent to zero), the first assertion of question 24 is
false, even for smooth complex quintic threefolds. It is also false if the
doubtful glyph is read as algebraic triviality itself. The implication
from $\tau$-triviality to numerical triviality remains true.

lem:B2-mumford.title: Proved from Mumford; moving pairs and two-forms
lem:B2-mumford.statement:
\label{lem:B2-mumford}
Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex surface, let
$\omega\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)$, and let $T$ be smooth and integral.
For a morphism $f:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^d S$, write $f^*\omega^{(d)}$
for Mumford's induced two-form. If $f,g:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^d S$
are families whose cycles are rationally equivalent at the generic
point after an algebraic extension of $\C(T)$, then
$f^*\omega^{(d)}=g^*\omega^{(d)}$.

thm:B2-square.title: Refuted with complete counterexample; both questions 25
thm:B2-square.statement:
\label{thm:B2-square}
Let $E/\overline\Q$ be the smooth elliptic curve
$y^2=x^3-x$ with origin $o$, and let $S=E_\C\times E_\C$.
Choose $p,q\in E(\C)$ such that the point $(p,q)$ is generic over
$\overline\Q$; for example choose $x(p),x(q)$ algebraically independent
over $\overline\Q$ and then choose the square roots defining their
$y$-coordinates. Put
\[
 a=\operatorname{pr}_1^*([p]-[o]),\quad
 b=\operatorname{pr}_2^*([q]-[o]),\quad
 D=a+b\in\mathrm{CH}^1(S).
\]
Then $D$ is algebraically trivial, but $D^2$ is nonzero, and indeed
nontorsion, in $\mathrm{CH}^2(S)$. Moreover
\[
 z=[(p,q)]-[(p,o)]-[(o,q)]+[(o,o)]
\]
is Albanese-trivial and nontorsion. Thus each question has a negative
answer with integral coefficients and with rational coefficients.

prop:B2-kernel.title: Proved; exact positive replacement on this surface
prop:B2-kernel.statement:
\label{prop:B2-kernel}
For $S=E_\C\times E_\C$, the kernel of
$\operatorname{alb}:\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\operatorname{Alb}(S)(\C)$
on degree-zero classes is generated by the cycles
\[
 z(p,q)=([p]-[o])\times([q]-[o]),\qquad p,q\in E(\C).
\]
Consequently over $\Q$ this kernel is spanned by squares of
algebraically trivial divisors. Products in the counterexample are
Albanese-trivial, although they need not be rationally trivial.

thm:B3-21.title: Proved from Gabber; universal degree-zero test
thm:B3-21.statement:
\label{thm:B3-21}
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal,
$X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and $i:Z\to X$.
The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair.
\item For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, the restriction
$H^0(X,F)\to H^0(Z,i^*F)$ is an isomorphism.
\item For every such $F$ and every $q\ge0$, the restriction
$H^q(X,F)\to H^q(Z,i^*F)$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
In particular $I$-adic completeness is sufficient, without a noetherian
hypothesis. The quantifier ``every sheaf'' cannot be replaced by ``one
fixed sheaf'' in the degree-zero test.

thm:B3-fujiwara.title: Known with checked application; the distinct completion theorem
thm:B3-fujiwara.statement:
\label{thm:B3-fujiwara}
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, let
$\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion, and let
$U\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an open subset containing
$\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$.
Put $\widehat U=U\times_A\widehat A$ and let
$\pi:\widehat U\to U$ be the projection.
For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and every $q\ge0$,
\[
 H^q(U,F)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
 H^q(\widehat U,\pi^*F).
\]

thm:B3-flat-crys.title: Known with checked deduction; subjects 1 and 8
thm:B3-flat-crys.statement:
\label{thm:B3-flat-crys}
For any scheme $X$, let
$a_X:\operatorname{Sh}((\operatorname{Sch}/X)_{\mathrm{fppf}})
\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ be the comparison morphism.
For every bounded below complex $K$ of abelian \'etale sheaves,
\[
 K\simeq Ra_{X,*}a_X^*K,
 \qquad
 R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},K)
 \simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{fppf}},a_X^*K).
\]
There is no invertibility condition on the torsion in this assertion.

For the crystalline addition to subject 1 and the connection addition
to subject 8, let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power ring with a prime
$p$ nilpotent in $A$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, let $Y\to S$
be smooth, and put $X=Y\times_A A/I$. If $\mathcal F$ is a crystal
in quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules, its value $\mathcal F_Y$
has a canonical integrable connection and
\[
 R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/S),\mathcal F)
 \simeq R\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F_Y\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}).
\]

thm:B3-approx.title: Known with checked deduction; subject 13
thm:B3-approx.statement:
\label{thm:B3-approx}
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $A$ a noetherian G-ring. Given
polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$, a solution
$\widehat a\in\widehat A^n$ in the $I$-adic completion, and $N\ge1$,
there is an exact solution $a\in A^n$ with
$a\equiv\widehat a\pmod{I^N\widehat A}$.

If $A=R$ is a henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$,
and the fraction field extension $\operatorname{Frac}\widehat R/
\operatorname{Frac}R$ is separable in positive characteristic, there
are constants $c,b\ge1$, depending on the finite polynomial system,
such that every solution modulo $t^{cn+b}$ is congruent modulo $t^n$
to an exact solution in $R$, for every $n\ge1$.

thm:B3-topos.title: Known and refuted in general; subject 14
thm:B3-topos.statement:
\label{thm:B3-topos}
A small site with finite limits whose coverings admit finite
refinements has enough points. An unrestricted Grothendieck topos
need not have even one point.

thm:B3-raynaud-flatness.title: Known with complete checked deduction; Raynaud's flatness criterion
thm:B3-raynaud-flatness.statement:
\label{thm:B3-raynaud-flatness}
Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $F$ be
a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. For $g:T\to S$, write
$f_T:X\times_S T\to T$ for the base-changed morphism and $F_T$ for
the pullback of $F$ to $X\times_S T$.
Suppose $F$ satisfies Raynaud's property $W$: there is
a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $Q$ such that,
for every $g:T\to S$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module $M$,
there are natural isomorphisms
\[
 (f_T)_*(F_T\otimes f_T^*M)
    \simeq\mathcal H\!om_{\mathcal O_T}(g^*Q,M).
\]
Then formation of $f_*F$ commutes with every base change if and only if
$Q$ is finite locally free. In that case $f_*F\simeq Q^\vee$.
If $F$ is also flat over $S$, this is cohomological flatness in dimension
zero in Raynaud's terminology.

thm:B3-picard.title: Known with checked deduction; subject 17
thm:B3-picard.statement:
\label{thm:B3-picard}
Let $S$ be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with perfect
residue field, and let $f:C\to S$ be a proper flat relative curve.
Assume $C$ is regular and $f_*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_S$.
